title: A biophysics-informed protein language model designs functional GFP variants
summary: Mutational Effect Transfer Learning (METL) combines transformer pretraining on simulated protein biophysics with fine-tuning on experimental sequence–function data. Using only 64 experimental GFP examples, the authors designed 20 previously untested variants and measured their fluorescence; 16 showed measurable fluorescence, although none was brighter than wild-type GFP. The result demonstrates functional design under a small-data setup, not improved brightness over wild type. The result was present in the bioRxiv version posted 2024-03-17; the GEM@ICLR 2024 workshop paper provides the detailed 20-variant assay report, and the later journal version is the same study.
ai_technology: Mutational Effect Transfer Learning (METL), a transformer protein language model pretrained on simulated biophysical features and fine-tuned on experimental data

evidence.tested: Twenty METL-designed GFP variants were synthesized and experimentally measured; 16 showed measurable fluorescence, but none exceeded wild-type brightness.
evidence.unknown: The panel contains 20 designed variants in a specific GFP task; the result does not show improvement over wild-type brightness or establish general performance across protein families.
evidence.ai_role: METL-Local was pretrained on simulated GFP sequence/biophysical data, fine-tuned using 64 experimental examples, and used with sequence optimization to select variants for wet-lab testing.

source_review.scope: Primary bioRxiv v1 indexed abstract, posting date and affiliation metadata; primary GEM@ICLR workshop paper full text with methods and experimental outcomes.
